name: Text Embeddings Inference (TEI)
notable_features: A whole engine class of its own: embedding, reranking and sequence-classification serving. Nobody confuses this with a generative engine, which is exactly why HuggingFace built it

Rust core with a Python router; the README claims no model graph compilation step, small docker images and fast boot times, and sells 'true serverless' on the back of that - a real operational advantage over the PyTorch engines because cold-start is short
Token-based dynamic batching rather than request-count batching, which is the correct unit when inputs have wildly different token lengths
Two weight-loading paths: safetensors AND onnx, plus ONNX Runtime for CPU. This is unusual and it is why TEI runs where a torch-based server will not
Optimized transformer path using Flash Attention, Candle and cuBLASLt; local builds go through `cargo install --path router -F candle-cuda` (or -F candle-cuda-turing for Turing)
Metal support for local execution on Macs
Production signals baked in: distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus metrics, gRPC alongside REST, and Swagger/OpenAPI docs at /docs
Covers FlagEmbedding, Jina, GTE, E5, BGE-class models plus SPLADE sparse pooling and sequence classifiers for reranking
v1.9 line: v1.9.4 released 2026-09-15, last push 2026-09-29, 5069 stars, 457 open issues
hardware_caveats: THE HARDWARE MATRIX IS THE RECORD. Published docker image table, v1.9 line: CPU x86_64 and aarch64; Volta x86_64 explicitly NOT SUPPORTED; Turing (T4, RTX 2000) image exists but is labelled experimental; Ampere 8.0 and 8.6, Ada Lovelace, Hopper images are the supported CUDA targets; Blackwell 100 (B200/GB200), 120 (RTX 50-series) and 121 (DGX Spark GB10) images are all labelled experimental

The README states plainly that GPUs with CUDA compute capability < 7.5 are not supported, naming V100, Titan V and the GTX 1000 series. If you have a V100 - still extremely common in inference fleets - TEI does not run and that is deliberate, not a bug
NVIDIA drivers must be compatible with CUDA 12.2 or higher
Flash Attention is turned OFF by default on the Turing image because of precision issues; you must set USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=True to get FA v1 back, and it is v1 not v2
CUDA feature flags are per-architecture, so the source build requires you to know your compute capability before `cargo install` - you cannot build one binary for a mixed fleet
ROCm is a documented but narrower path: separate images for AMD Instinct MI200 and MI300 series only, with its own guide. No ROCm support is claimed for consumer AMD parts

Apple Silicon local use runs on CPU/Metal via the CPU build; the README's own wording is 'for ARM64 hosts without NVIDIA GPUs ... Inference runs on CPU cores'. Do not read 'Metal support' as Metal-accelerated GPU embedding serving
Architectures ahead of the supported list (Blackwell) run experimental images - i.e. unsupported
TEI serves embeddings and rerankers only. Point it at a generative model and it is the wrong tool; that is not a limitation so much as the boundary of the class
best_for: Serving embeddings and rerankers in production, especially where the vector DB is the bottleneck and embedding throughput is the real constraint
Serverless or autoscaling deployments, because no graph compilation and small images are first-class design goals rather than accidents
CPU-only or ARM64 embedding serving via the ONNX path, which is the cheapest credible way to embed at scale without a GPU
Heterogeneous fleets where embedding models are small and the per-image CUDA specialisation is annoying - pick the right tag per SKU
Teams already on HuggingFace infrastructure, since the model and pooling conventions match
avoid_for: V100 or older, and Blackwell-class parts on anything but experimental images
AMD consumer GPUs (RX cards) - ROCm coverage is data-centre MI-series only
Expecting the Mac path to be GPU-accelerated; it is a CPU build
notes: The embedding/reranking niche's reference runtime, and the answer to 'which engine do I use for retrieval infrastructure'. Rust core + ONNX/Candle/CUDA paths + token-based dynamic batching + explicit per-architecture image matrix makes it the best-documented hardware story in this slice. Related but distinct: [[niche-infinity]] (multi-backend, more model coverage, slower cadence) and [[niche-colbert]] (late interaction, a different compute shape entirely).
